clue.text: Very much at home before a meal

parts.note: far means very much, as in far better
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone is very much a homebody before a meal is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Farina is a fine flour or meal made from cereal grain, so meal is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Man perhaps excised start of passage

indicators.note: excised start of tells us to cut away the opening letter of the word for passage

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: An editor has cut the opening of a passage of text.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Women held in roadside robbery in the first instance talk with officer in pairs

indicators.note: held in says the letter for women sits inside the word for roadside robbery

parts.note: toby is old thieves' slang for highway robbery, as in the high toby

indicators.note: in the first instance points to the opening letters of the three words that follow it

explanation.surface: A report of a highway hold-up involving women, followed by a chat with a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Toby is old thieves' slang for highway robbery (the high toby), unfamiliar to most solvers; 'officer' looks like a piece but only lends its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals entering the ark two by two came in pairs, so the phrase is an idiom for in pairs.

clue.text: Most dry areas limit journey time

indicators.note: limit here means bound on either side, so the letters for areas enclose the journey

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so areas is the plural AS
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Desert regions put a cap on how long a trip can take.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means dry, so its superlative means driest or most dry.

clue.text: Excited learners following notes at English Department

indicators.note: following says the learners come after the notes in the answer

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale, so two notes give TITI
L is the learner plate sign, so two learners are LL

explanation.surface: Students got worked up after reading memos at the English department.
explanation.definitionFit: Titillated means pleasurably stimulated or aroused, a close synonym of excited.

clue.text: A new northern university's in style every year

indicators.note: in says the letters before it go inside the word for style

parts.note: a perm is a hairstyle
U is the abbreviation for university; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A fresh northern university is fashionable every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for each year, used in English for yearly amounts such as salaries.

clue.text: 24D's beast eating another by a railway

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: eating says one animal swallows the other, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a cow is a beast of the farm
another beast, here an ass

explanation.surface: A wild animal devours a second creature beside a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless creature of New Guinea and Australia, related to the emu.

clue.text: 24D's salesman, one parking in reverse

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: in reverse says the assembled letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
I is the Roman numeral one
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman, a single car parked badly while backing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Piper is a name for several wading shorebirds, notably the sandpiper.

clue.text: Olympian chap runs about

parts.note: a chap is a he, a male
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a is a dictionary abbreviation for about, approximately

explanation.surface: An athlete at the Olympics jogs around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' looks like an athlete; here it means a god living on Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera, queen of the Greek gods, was one of the twelve deities dwelling on Mount Olympus.

clue.text: 24D's Christopher Marlowe's end

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: Kit is a short form of Christopher, as with the playwright Kit Marlowe

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of the playwright's surname

explanation.surface: A reference to how the Elizabethan playwright met his death.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Marlowe was commonly called Kit; take KIT and add the last letter of Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: The kite is a bird of prey with a forked tail, such as the red kite.

clue.text: 24D's pompous Republican conceals capital

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: conceals says the capital city is hidden inside the other letters

parts.note: budge is an old adjective meaning pompous or solemn
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: A self-important American Republican is hiding money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests money, but it is a capital city, Riga. BUDGE (an archaic adjective, pompous) plus R wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet, popular as a cage pet.

clue.text: 24D's the usual nonsense

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: par is the normal or usual standard, as in par for the course
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone complains that this is the same old rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The parrot is a brightly coloured tropical bird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Bad loser admits procedure left examples to be followed

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the rearranged letters take the other pieces inside
bad here means poorly formed, so the letters of loser are rearranged

parts.note: a mode is a way or procedure of doing something

explanation.surface: A sore loser concedes that the method left behind good examples to copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges LOSER to ROLES, which then 'admits' MODE and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Role models are people whose behaviour others look up to and imitate.

clue.text: 24D's sunfish?

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: the sun is a star, so the first half of the word gives STAR
the ling is a fish of the cod family, so the second half of the word gives LING

explanation.surface: A question about a big ocean fish called the sunfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'sunfish' into sun (a star) and fish (ling); the question mark flags this split.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common songbird with glossy speckled plumage, famous for vast murmurations.

clue.text: 24D's flower trick

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A bird is said to use a floral deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but a thing that flows: a river, here the Fal, in Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The falcon is a fast bird of prey, such as the peregrine.

clue.text: Adherent of retuning Liberal subordinate

indicators.note: retuning, read as returning, says the little word of is turned back to front

parts.note: lower means subordinate, of lesser rank

explanation.surface: A supporter of a Liberal who is re-tuning a junior instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retuning' appears to be a printing slip for 'returning', the reversal signal on the little word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or disciple, one who follows a leader or cause.

clue.text: 24D's outlaw cheers Frenchman

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
M stands for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title

explanation.surface: A bandit raises a toast to a man from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlaw' looks like a noun (a bandit) but is the verb, to ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken.

clue.text: A companion paper for e.g. Ofqual, Ofsted

parts.note: a crony is a close companion
MS is short for manuscript, a paper

explanation.surface: A friend writes a document about the English school regulators.
explanation.walkthrough: Ofqual and Ofsted are English bodies regulating exams and schools; their names are formed from the initial parts of longer titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Words made from the initial parts of longer names are acronyms, and these two regulators are examples.

clue.text: Dances thus on pitch when in the ascendant

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising or ascending means reading the letters from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: so means thus
re means on, concerning
to lob is to pitch or throw high

explanation.surface: Dancing on a football pitch when one's team is on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The bolero is a Spanish dance in triple time, so the plural gives dances.

clue.text: 24D's ring of fire?

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: of here means made of or belonging to, so the burning word comes ahead of the round letter

parts.note: flaming means on fire, burning
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A circle of flames, as in the famous song.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'ring of fire' as a flaming O.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

clue.text: Catch fish in the Netherlands

indicators.note: in says the fish's name sits inside the letters for the Netherlands

parts.note: NL is the international vehicle code for the Netherlands
the ai, or ayu, is a small edible Japanese river fish

explanation.surface: Landing a fish in Dutch waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like part of a fishing scene but is the definition; the fish is the obscure ai, a small Japanese sweetfish.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a criminal is to catch or pin them down, an informal verb sense.

clue.text: 24D's sending off: way out for player, to begin with

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: out for says the letters for way leave the card and the next letter takes their place

parts.note: a red card in football means a player is sent off
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

indicators.note: to begin with points to the first letter of the word player

explanation.surface: A football dismissal: the exit route for a player at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a red card sends a player off; RD (road, a way) is swapped for P, the start of 'player'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is an old country name for the goldfinch, from its red face.

clue.text: Notorious Australian bishop accepted holy books

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
A is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange
NT is the New Testament, a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: An infamous Australian bishop took on scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter or out-and-out, used of a notorious rogue or an arrant fool.

clue.text: 24D's number, say, Hieroglyph paid back after court

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: after says the reversed letters follow the word for court

parts.note: to court a sweetheart is to woo

indicators.note: back says the pieces before it are read in reverse order

parts.note: EG, for example, means say
the setter Hieroglyph refers to himself as I
PD is the abbreviation for paid

explanation.surface: The setter describes a sum he paid back after a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name means I; NO, EG, I, PD read 'back' give DPIGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood pigeon is a large grey pigeon common in European woods and gardens.

clue.text: 24D's pub grub after losing key game

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: G is a musical key
RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Bar food after a defeat in a crucial match.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G (a key) and RU (rugby union) from GRUB to leave B.
explanation.definitionFit: The barb is a breed of domestic pigeon, originally from Barbary.

clue.text: Try restraining right winger

clue.text: 24D's learner in lake

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: A student driver has ended up in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Merle is an old literary and Scottish name for the blackbird.

clue.text: 24D's my second outburst

definitions.note: 24D refers to the answer at 24 down, a winged creature; the 's stands for is

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my
a mo is a moment, a second
a rant is an angry outburst

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that this is their second tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation (as in 'my!'), giving COR, British slang of surprise.
